turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Hi, I'm Jess, the nurse. Just need a blood pressure before Doctor Shah comes in. You hanging in there?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Barely. Been in that waiting room forever. I checked my pressure at home this morning, it was 152 over 90.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Okay. Right now I've got 136 over 78, and your pulse is 76. I'll tell her you're set.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Whatever. Can we move.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr. Keller, I'm Doctor Shah. Sorry you got stuck out there. What brought you in today?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): This. Left side of my chest. It burns, and there's a few little blisters. Two days now.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Burning and blisters. Walk me through how it feels.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Like a hot iron sitting on the skin. It stays on the one side, doesn't jump across. Uh, if my shirt rubs it, forget it. And I feel wiped out.
[SEG0009] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm Dana, I come by the house to help. He's been sleeping badly since this started, up half the night.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. That's right. I can't sleep with this thing.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry. Any fever with it, or chills?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about healing, do little cuts drag on for you or do they close up okay?
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He caught his forearm on a cabinet last week. The cut healed in five days. Looked totally normal.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): It was fine. Healed. Can we get back to the burning, I'm tired of sitting here.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of course. Way back, did you have chickenpox as a kid?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. I was maybe seven. Whole family had it. I remember the itching.
[SEG0018] person_4 (CAREGIVER): He takes a blood pressure pill too, lisinapril, ten milligrams. But he does not take the tablets on Sundays.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): It's lisinopril, not whatever you said. And it's not Sundays. Err, I skip Saturdays. Once a day the other days, by mouth.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Got it. Lisinopril ten milligrams once a day, and Saturday is the day you skip. How long's the blood pressure been a thing?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Years. Five-ish years. Don't ask me the month, I have no idea. It's still ongoing.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's okay, we don't need the exact month. Mind if I look at the rash? Shirt up just a little.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Ugh. Yeah. Easy. It hurts when you touch near it.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): There's a small cluster of blisters on the left chest, kind of in a band, and it stops right at the midline. The skin around them is red. Lungs sound clear when I listen.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): So. What is it. Just say it.

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): I think this is shingles, herpes zoster. Burning on one side, blisters in a strip, and you had chickenpox as a child. That's my working read, we haven't proved it with a test.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Shingles. My neighbor had that. He complained for a month. Also his dog barked all night, not that you care.
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Frank's daughter is pregnant. She's due in the spring, and she was planning to come over tomorrow.

[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then let's keep her away until the blisters crust over and dry up. The fluid can pass chickenpox to somebody who never had it, and we really don't want that in pregnancy. Wash your hands, don't share towels, keep the rash covered.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm seventy four and I don't get to see my own daughter. Fantastic.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Only for a short bit, till it crusts. I am going to start an antiviral today. Valacyclovir, a thousand milligrams by mouth, three times a day, for seven days. Better to start now.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Three times a day. I'll mess it up. I'm already lousy about Saturdays with the other pill.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): This one you shouldn't skip. Dana, if you can help him track the doses, that would be great.
[SEG0034] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll put an alarm on my phone. He's not gonna sleep though, the pain is bad.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): You can take acetaminophen by mouth for the pain, whatever the usual over the counter amount is on the bottle. I'm not adding a second prescription today.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Bottle dose. Sure. I just want the burning to stop.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it does not settle, we might do a scan, but I'm not ordering one today. Let's see you back in two weeks.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. And a scan if it doesn't. Okay I guess.
[SEG0039] person_4 (CAREGIVER): What if the blisters spread before then, do I call?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. If they spread quickly, or he gets short of breath, or the pain suddenly jumps, don't sit on it for two weeks. Call us or go to urgent care.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not sitting in an ER for a rash. I'm exhausted. We done?

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nearly. The valacyclovir will be waiting at the front desk, start it today. If it upsets your stomach, take it with a little food. And keep that rash covered if anyone stops by.
[SEG0043] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll tell his daughter not to come. I'll grab the prescription on the way out.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Tell her I'm not making it up. It actually burns.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the slip. Just so it's on the note, the blood pressure I got was 136 over 78.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I already said it was 152 over 90 at home. But sure, write your number.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Home numbers and office numbers don't always match, and that's okay. We'll use today's 136 over 78. Hope you get some rest, Mr. Keller.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Thanks. I guess.
[SEG0049] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Come on Frank, car's out front. We'll stop for the medicine.

spec.situation: Older person with burning pain on one side of the chest and a few blisters for two days; remembers chickenpox as a child; doctor prescribes antiviral today and gives infection advice about contact with a pregnant relative.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Present burning left chest pain, blisters, 2 days, worse with shirt rubbing supported; severity 'severe' and category 'neurological' not stated.
bad.text: Burning chest pain (category=neurological, status=present, severity=severe, duration=2 days, onset=two days ago, temporality=current, body_site=left chest, associated_symptoms=blisters, aggravating_factors=shirt rubbing, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Transcript states he skips lisinopril on Saturdays; this is presented as known behavior, not unresolved uncertainty.

omissions.text: Current blood pressure medicine adherence detail was clarified and resolved: caregiver incorrectly said he skips Sundays, but patient clarified he skips Saturdays; this was confirmed by the doctor, so it should not remain as an unresolved uncertainty/disagreement.
Home blood pressure reading reported by the patient was 152/90 this morning.
Rash pain/allodynia detail: touching near the rash hurts.
Rash distribution detail on exam/symptoms: it is in a band/strip and stops at the midline, staying on one side and not crossing over.
Negative finding asked and answered: chills were denied along with fever.
Relevant history supporting assessment: patient had chickenpox in childhood, around age 7.
Valacyclovir start timing and administration advice: it should be started today, will be waiting at the front desk, and if it upsets his stomach he should take it with a little food.
